evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Validate data sources before publishing — numbers must be right, definitions consistent, and formatting clean...Review your own work before handoff — check filters, totals, joins, and formatting against a Definition of Done
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Data validation, documentation, naming conventions, and BI governance dominate the responsibilities throughout with no velocity/speed language present.
evidence.domain_risk: Secretlab is an international gaming chair brand seating over a million users worldwide
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Consumer e-commerce/gaming chair brand where errors affect internal dashboards and business decisions with limited, recoverable consequences and no regulatory or financial-reporting framing.
evidence.collaboration_width: Logistics; Marketing; Finance; E-commerce; Ops; CRM
evidence.data_team_maturity: Within the Data team, you'll collaborate with our Data Engineers throughout the delivery cycle...following the naming conventions, certified sources, and dashboard standards that keep BI consistent
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: An existing Data team with Data Engineers, certified data sources, and established BI governance standards indicate a functioning, moderately mature data function.
evidence.jd_authorship: Administer and maintain Tableau Server — monitor performance, manage user access and permissions, handle platform-level configuration, and ensure uptime and reliability
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Precise technical detail (Tableau Server administration, LOD calculations, fact/dimension marts) gives a clear picture of daily work.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: You'll be a trusted partner to a variety of teams including Logistics, Marketing, Finance, and turn their reporting needs into effective BI products
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: Spans Logistics, Marketing, Finance, E-commerce, Ops, and CRM with no single dominant orientation among these business functions.
evidence.autonomy_level: Translate routine business questions into well-scoped analytical deliverables — clarify the ask, agree on metrics, and ship within timelines
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: Responsibilities are scoped around receiving and delivering against stakeholder requests within a Definition of Done, rather than setting overall data strategy.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: No AI tool usage or AI-adjacent data infrastructure work is mentioned anywhere in the JD.
evidence.testing_framing: Validate data sources before publishing — numbers must be right, definitions consistent, and formatting clean. Document dashboard logic, metric definitions, and data source lineage
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Data validation and quality ownership are framed as an explicit, owned responsibility with concrete action verbs (validate, document, flag issues), not just a tool in a skills list.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: Flag data quality issues, deprecated sources, and broken dashboards proactively rather than waiting for them to be reported
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Moderate framing — reliability and correctness of dashboards are emphasized throughout, but the fear is bad dashboards/broken pipelines rather than compliance or regulatory exposure.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Maintain and refresh existing dashboards — fix broken visualisations, update metric logic, and tune performance
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Mix of building new dashboards for product launches and maintaining/fixing existing BI products, with maintenance work described in more detail — leaning fix_scale.
evidence.loss_aversion: Flag data quality issues, deprecated sources, and broken dashboards proactively — moderate reliability/trust framing without compliance or regulatory risk language.

responsibilities: Build new dashboards and visualisations for stakeholder requests, especially around new product launches and campaigns.
Maintain and refresh existing dashboards — fix broken visualisations, update metric logic, and tune performance.
Pair with Data Engineers on data mart requirements — write requirements, validate outputs in UAT, and confirm correctness before publishing.
Run short data literacy sessions or walkthroughs with stakeholders to lift self-service usage.
Triage incoming data and dashboard requests — clarify scope, estimate effort, and queue them sensibly.
Sit in on stakeholder meetings to surface upcoming reporting needs early.
Document metric definitions and dashboard logic in Confluence as work is delivered.
Review your own work before handoff — check filters, totals, joins, and formatting against a Definition of Done.
Build and maintain dashboards, reports, and data sources that stakeholders can confidently use to make decisions.
Translate routine business questions into well-scoped analytical deliverables — clarify the ask, agree on metrics, and ship within timelines.
Validate data sources before publishing — numbers must be right, definitions consistent, and formatting clean.
Document dashboard logic, metric definitions, and data source lineage so others can maintain the work.
Support self-service adoption — answer metric clarifications, run dashboard walkthroughs, and help business users get to the insight on their own.
Flag data quality issues, deprecated sources, and broken dashboards proactively rather than waiting for them to be reported.
Administer and maintain Tableau Server — monitor performance, manage user access and permissions, handle platform-level configuration, and ensure uptime and reliability for the wider organisation.
Work directly with business teams (E-commerce, Marketing, Ops, Finance, CRM) to understand reporting needs and turn them into deliverables.
Write clear Jira tickets and dashboard requirements so engineers and reviewers can act without ambiguity.

Work closely with Data Engineers throughout delivery — articulate data requirements precisely, contribute to mart and data source design discussions, and validate outputs in UAT end-to-end before anything reaches a stakeholder.

Tailor explanations to the audience — analysts, managers, and VPs each need a different level of detail. Take feedback well, iterate quickly, and close the loop with stakeholders once changes are shipped.
Contribute to BI governance — naming conventions, certified data sources, dashboard standards — by following them consistently and flagging gaps.
